title: Docker compose integration tests: dump container logs before stop() on failure
answers: Docker compose integration test times out with no container output
How do I see docker compose logs when an MLflow integration test fails?
Why are container logs missing after a compose integration test fails?
health endpoint not ready within timeout in docker integration test
body:
Symptom: A docker-based integration test (e.g. PostgreSQL backend) times out waiting for the server's /health endpoint in CI, and the failure shows no container output.
Root cause: tests/docker/test_integrations.py:test_backend_and_artifact_store_integration used `with compose:`, so teardown ran before any failure output was available, and removing the containers also removed their logs.
Fix pattern: Call compose.start() explicitly inside try, and in `except Exception:` call compose.get_logs(), print stdout/stderr, then re-raise. Call compose.stop() in `finally:`.
Constraints: Logs are only captured on the failure path; the success path should not print them. Testcontainers' get_logs() relies on compose command output captured via subprocess.run(capture_output=True), so keep the dump before stop().
Applies: Tests in tests/docker/ that use testcontainers DockerCompose and need diagnosable failures.
applies: Tests under tests/docker/ that build a testcontainers DockerCompose environment; does not cover non-compose container setups.
says: Automated integration test times out in CI without showing any container output logs.
Print backend container logs directly into CI output whenever integration test runs fail.
Container logs disappear after health check timeouts because test teardown removes the containers.
Failed database integration tests provide zero diagnostic output explaining why the server stalled.
Retain and display container console errors before shutting down failed integration test environments.
search: In tests/docker/ integration tests using testcontainers DockerCompose, call compose.start() inside try, dump container stdout and stderr via compose.get_logs() in except Exception: before re-raising, and call compose.stop() in finally:. This prevents CI test timeouts on the /health endpoint from losing container logs during teardown in tests like tests/docker/test_integrations.py:test_backend_and_artifact_store_integration. Logs must be dumped only on failure before stop() runs, and this guidance applies to testcontainers DockerCompose environments rather than non-compose setups.
